first.rationale: The current situation shows simultaneous declines in activation (6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (4% QoQ). Memory_31 and memory_86 directly demonstrate that signup simplification and shortened onboarding both improved activation and completion rates. These interventions are low-risk (no retention trade-offs unlike promotional_pricing per memory_73), have proven durable lift, and directly address both metrics currently declining. Verifying these two will confirm whether the original effect sizes and mechanisms remain valid under current conditions. Promotional pricing is rejected despite competitive pressure because memory_73 explicitly flagged material 30-day retention harm, which conflicts with maximizing sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Enterprise sales assist is relevant but memory_44 indicates it's effective for pipeline quality, not activation recovery. Referral incentives work for established customers (memory_57) but don't address the root activation decline. Activation messaging (memory_91) is secondary; fixing the onboarding funnel first creates more accounts to engage. A standard_experiment scope is appropriate: large enough to detect signal on both activation and completion metrics, guarded enough to halt if unexpected downstream effects emerge.

final.rationale: Archive verification confirms both interventions deliver measurable, sustainable gains. Memory_31 shows signup simplification drove +9% activation and +4% qualified revenue in SMB with only -1% retention risk. Memory_86 shows shortened onboarding achieved +13% completion, -2.1 days time-to-value, and +3% retention lift—a rare case of simultaneous activation and retention gains. Current state: activation and onboarding completion are both down 4-6% QoQ. Simplification directly targets both declining metrics and aligns with primary objective (sustainable long-term qualified revenue) because exp_86 data explicitly shows retention improved, not harmed. The -1% retention dip in exp_31 is minimal and offset by qualified revenue gain. Onboarding simplification is lower-risk than promotional pricing (which materially harmed retention per memory_73) and addresses root friction rather than acquisition mechanics. The experiment should apply simplification across both signup (exp_31 pattern) and onboarding flow (exp_86 pattern) to compound effect. Standard_experiment scale allows detection of interaction effects and downstream retention impact while remaining guarded enough to pause if atypical harm emerges.
